record.file_problem: Contains stray editorial placeholder text, but the full paper and supplementary information are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling in a new setting: simulation-to-real transfer learning for polymer-property prediction, as the computational database grows.
record.gate_note: The relevant results concern scaling of downstream generalisation error with computational-database size in Sim2Real transfer learning. The polymer database analyses and scaling results merely cited from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fits E = D n^-α + C to the downstream experimental-property error of MLPs pretrained on simulated polymer data and fine-tuned, as source-data size n grows from about 10^2 to 10^5. That is a power-law test in a non-language transfer/fine-tuning regime, which is what V5 names. V6 concerns downstream tasks of language models, and no language model is studied here, so the rows are linked to V5 only.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that Sim2Real-transferred models' real-world error falls as a power law in the size of the computational database, supporting 'more is better'. They add that transferability is limited by the quantity and quality of experimental data, that some curves plateau, and that scaling is measured only within a finite polymer subset.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a five-hidden-layer multilayer perceptron for Sim2Real transfer, scaling computational source-dataset size and measuring downstream experimental-property generalisation error; it does not scale language-model parameters, tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Scaling results differ across source and target property tasks. The authors report convergence for thermal conductivity and linear thermal expansion around n = 10^4 and identify experimental-data quantity and quality as factors affecting transferability.
record.problems: The reported scaling criterion is an area-ratio threshold, and the text does not provide uncertainty estimates for the scaling results. Many task-specific outcomes are described qualitatively or as aggregate counts rather than with separate numerical curves. Some target datasets are small; for example, the paper states that only 39 experimental thermal-conductivity values were available.
record.rows_left_out: No additional relevant results left out. The article's other database and polymer-property findings do not test the claim versions.

untested.parts: No language-model pretraining loss against parameters, tokens or compute.
No extrapolation from small fits to much larger runs; curves are fitted and evaluated over the same n range.
Architecture is fixed: a five-layer MLP (512, 256, 128, 64, 32 neurons).
Only source-data size is varied; no scaling in model size or compute. Image, video and repeated-data regimes are not tested.
No comparison of fitting choices or schedules.

missing.what: Per-task fitted α and transfer gap C, and any goodness-of-fit check of the power law against alternatives
missing.locator: Fig. 4c; Methods, Transfer learning workflow and scaling analysis

missing.what: Per-pair significance matrix and the count of pairs with negative transfer

record.verdict_notes: The power-law form is assumed (Eq. 1). 'Significance' is an area ratio of at most 0.95 against the scratch MAE over n from 10^2 to 10^5, with no uncertainty and no fit diagnostics. Uses a single small MLP. The authors build on their own prior Sim2Real scaling work (Minami et al. 2025).

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test language-model held-out pretraining loss against parameter count, token count, or compute.
It does not test whether power laws fitted on small language-model runs predict much larger runs.
It does not test compute-optimal allocation between language-model parameters and training tokens.
It does not test the effect of language-model architecture shape on loss.
Tests Sim2Real transfer learning for polymer properties, not image/video models, repeated data, or other training regimes.
Tests downstream polymer-property prediction as computational source-database size changes; does not test downstream performance against language-model pretraining loss or model size.
Does not test how language-model scaling exponents or compute-optimal splits vary with parameter counting, training schedules, or fitting choices.

rows.subject: conventional multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated Sim2Real transfer as the PolyOmics computational source-dataset size increased.

conditions.value: estimated-curve area divided by scratch-learning baseline area ≤ 0.95

rows.measure: Number of transfer scenarios showing significant scaling
rows.baseline: Scratch learning on experimental data; area ratio threshold ≤ 0.95
rows.value: 635 of the 43×61 transfer scenarios showed notable scaling.
rows.locator: Scaling law of Sim2Real transfer learning; Fig. 4b; Methods, Transfer learning workflow and scaling analysis
rows.note: Aggregate count across all source-target task combinations.
rows.check: 635 of 43×61 = 2,623 pairs is about 24%, so about 76% of source–target pairs showed no significant scaling. 'Significant' means only an area ratio ≤0.95 against a flat scratch baseline, not a test of power-law fit quality. Recorded as observed; it should be partial.

relationships.condition: Same-property Sim2Real transfer (density, refractive index, Tg, Cp) and selected named targets
relationships.reason: Error falls with source-data size, following the fitted power law with offset, and beats scratch learning (r2, r3, r4, r7-r10); exponents are given only as a range.
relationships.display_finding: Transfer error decreased with source-data size along fitted power laws with offsets and remained below errors from training from scratch.

relationships.condition: Thermal conductivity and linear thermal expansion targets
relationships.reason: Curves saturate around n = 10^4, where small or noisy experimental data cap the gain (r5, r6).
relationships.display_finding: Curves saturated around 10⁴ examples, with gains constrained by small or noisy experimental datasets.

relationships.reason: Only about 24% of pairs pass a lenient area-ratio criterion; the best sources scale for 33–48% of targets; under 7% show negative transfer (r1, r11-r15).
relationships.display_finding: About 24% of source–target pairs passed a lenient area-ratio criterion, the best sources scaled for 33–48% of targets, and under 7% showed negative transfer.
